result.summary: This part of the zig-regex 0.2.1 diff adds generated Unicode property tables, a UTF-8 byte-range lowering for character classes, and changes to the NFA VM that reuse buffers and fix capture handling. I checked every added and changed line for I/O, network use, process execution, environment access, encoded payloads and build-time hooks, and found none. All of the code is pure regex-engine logic.

findings.title: Generated Unicode property tables
findings.detail: The new file is a large generated table of Unicode 17.0.0 Script, Script_Extensions and binary-property ranges, used for \p{...} matching. It holds only numeric range structs, StaticStringMap name lookups and a switch that returns slices. Nothing in it is encoded or executable, and it has no I/O or side effects. Spot checks agree with known UCD data, for example ASCII letters mapped to Latin (75) and White_Space ranges.

findings.title: UTF-8 class lowering
findings.detail: The new file lowers code-point class sets into UTF-8/WTF-8 byte-range sequences, the standard utf8-ranges technique. It is pure computation over allocator-managed lists with no system access.

findings.title: VM scratch-buffer reuse and capture fixes
